title: Ladies of Soul: The Eighties
theme: The svengali decade. Rick James built the Mary Jane Girls from scratch. Prince built Vanity 6 — then rebuilt it as Apollonia 6 when the original lead walked out. Almost every major 1980s girl group was a male producer's creative project. The notable exception: Klymaxx, who played their own instruments, wrote their own material, and answered to nobody.
narrativePurpose: Trace the 1980s girl group arc from Prince's protégée factory through Rick James's Mary Jane Girls, the Weather Girls' disco-adjacent bombast, and Exposé's Miami freestyle — with Klymaxx standing apart as the decade's most self-directed female act. Purple Rain is the episode's axis: the year the svengali model reached its most cinematic expression.
toneProgression: The hits and the films that defined the era → the production machinery, the svengali figures, and the individuals who operated outside that system → the archival connections hiding inside the decade's most celebrated girl group moments

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-8-4 — the year Purple Rain is released, Apollonia 6's 'Sex Shooter' appears in the film, and Klymaxx release 'Meeting in the Ladies Room.' 1984: the svengali-produced girl group story reaches its most cinematic moment — and the most compelling alternative to that model announces itself.

rounds.name: RADIO HITS
rounds.description: The hits and films that defined the 1980s girl group era.

questions.question: Prince's protégée group Vanity 6 launched with which 1982 single — a provocative debut that announced a new era of production-driven girl group R&B?
choices: If a Girl Answers (Don't Hang Up)

metadata.fact: 'Nasty Girl' was Vanity 6's debut single in 1982 — written and produced by Prince, and built around the same blueprint he would refine through every protégée project that followed: provocative premise, tight funk production, female voices delivering his vision.
metadata.storyHook: 'Nasty Girl.' 1982. Vanity 6. Prince wrote it. Prince produced it. The voices were someone else's — but the blueprint was entirely his.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Nasty Girl' was Vanity 6's 1982 debut single, written and produced by Prince. Standard biographical knowledge.

questions.question: When Denise Matthews departed Prince's protégée project before Purple Rain began filming, which actress and singer replaced her as lead of the newly renamed Apollonia 6?

metadata.fact: Apollonia Kotero replaced Denise Matthews (Vanity) as the lead of Prince's protégée group — which was renamed Apollonia 6 — and appeared as Prince's love interest in Purple Rain (1984).
metadata.storyHook: Vanity left. Prince needed a new lead. Apollonia Kotero walked in. Apollonia 6. Purple Rain. One departure changed the entire shape of the project.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Apollonia Kotero replaced Denise Matthews as lead of the renamed Apollonia 6 and appeared in Purple Rain. Standard biographical knowledge.

questions.question: The Mary Jane Girls — Rick James's protégée group — scored their biggest hit with which 1985 recording, which reached the top of the R&B chart?

metadata.fact: 'In My House' was the Mary Jane Girls' biggest hit — reaching #1 on the R&B chart in 1985. Written and produced by Rick James, it was the clearest distillation of what he had built with the group: propulsive funk, seductive vocals, and an unmistakably Jamesian production identity.
metadata.storyHook: 'In My House.' 1985. #1 R&B. Everything Rick James built the Mary Jane Girls to be, in three and a half minutes.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'In My House' reached #1 R&B in 1985. Standard biographical knowledge.
metadata.hostNote: Rick James died August 6, 2004. The question addresses only his production role with the Mary Jane Girls — not his death or legal history.

questions.question: The Mary Jane Girls — who scored R&B hits including 'All Night Long' and 'In My House' — were created, written for, and produced entirely by which artist?

metadata.fact: Rick James conceived, created, wrote for, and produced the Mary Jane Girls — a protégée group he built in the image of his own musical aesthetic. Every song on their albums was a Rick James production.
metadata.storyHook: Rick James didn't just produce the Mary Jane Girls. He invented them. Every song, every production, every direction — that was Rick James working through another set of voices.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Rick James created, wrote, and produced the Mary Jane Girls. Standard biographical knowledge.
metadata.hostNote: Rick James died August 6, 2004. The question addresses only his production role — not his death or legal history.

questions.question: The Weather Girls announced themselves in 1982 with which impossibly exuberant recording — one of the decade's most instantly recognizable opening lines?
choices: Dear Santa (Bring Me a Man This Christmas)
No One Will Ever Love You

metadata.fact: 'It's Raining Men' (1982) established Martha Wash and Izora Armstead as The Weather Girls — a declaration of outsized personality that became one of the decade's most indestructible anthems.
metadata.storyHook: 'It's Raining Men.' 1982. Martha Wash and Izora Armstead. An opening line nobody forgets, from two singers who had been backing somebody else for years.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'It's Raining Men' was The Weather Girls' 1982 breakthrough hit. Standard biographical knowledge.

questions.question: Klymaxx — the all-female band who wrote and performed their own material — broke through with which 1984 recording that became one of R&B's most enduring party tracks?

metadata.fact: 'Meeting in the Ladies Room' (1984) was Klymaxx's commercial breakthrough — an all-female band that played their own instruments, wrote their own songs, and operated without a male svengali at the helm, making them a genuine counterpoint to the Mary Jane Girls and Vanity 6 model.
metadata.storyHook: 'Meeting in the Ladies Room.' 1984. Klymaxx. No Rick James. No Prince. They wrote it, they played it, they owned it.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Meeting in the Ladies Room' was Klymaxx's 1984 breakthrough. Standard biographical knowledge.

questions.question: Apollonia 6 — the group Prince assembled after Vanity 6's dissolution — performed their signature song 'Sex Shooter' in which landmark 1984 film?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — THE 1984 FILM FEATURING APOLLONIA 6

metadata.fact: Purple Rain (1984) featured Apollonia 6 performing 'Sex Shooter' — the song's primary commercial context. The film presented the entire Apollonia 6 project to a mass audience and made 'Sex Shooter' inseparable from its Purple Rain moment.
metadata.storyHook: Purple Rain. 1984. Apollonia 6 on stage. 'Sex Shooter.' The entire protégée project delivered to a global audience in a single scene.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Apollonia 6 performed 'Sex Shooter' in Purple Rain (1984). Standard biographical knowledge.
metadata.hostNote: Prince died April 21, 2016. The question addresses only the film and group — not his death.

reserve.question: Denise Matthews — who fronted Prince's protégée group before departing the project — performed under which stage name?

metadata.fact: Denise Matthews performed as 'Vanity' — the stage name Prince gave her — as the lead of Vanity 6. She departed the project before Purple Rain went into production.
metadata.storyHook: Her name was Denise Matthews. Prince called her Vanity. She was the original face of the protégée project — before she walked away.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Denise Matthews performed as 'Vanity' with Vanity 6. Standard biographical knowledge.
metadata.hostNote: Denise Matthews (Vanity) died February 15, 2016. The question addresses only her stage name — not her death.

reserve.question: Apollonia 6's only major single — featured in the film Purple Rain — was which provocatively titled recording?

metadata.fact: 'Sex Shooter' was Apollonia 6's defining recording — appearing in Purple Rain and introduced to a mass audience through the film's iconic performance scene. Like everything in the Apollonia 6 project, it was written and produced by Prince.
metadata.storyHook: 'Sex Shooter.' Purple Rain. The song that introduced Apollonia 6 to the world — inside a film that was impossible to ignore.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Sex Shooter' was Apollonia 6's major single, featured in Purple Rain. Standard biographical knowledge.

reserve.question: The Mary Jane Girls released their hit recordings on which Motown subsidiary label — named for the founder of the parent company?

metadata.fact: The Mary Jane Girls released their recordings on Gordy Records — a Motown subsidiary label named for Berry Gordy, the company's founder. Rick James's deal at Gordy gave him the platform to develop and release the group's catalog.
metadata.storyHook: Gordy Records. Named for Berry Gordy. The Mary Jane Girls were a Motown project — filtered through Rick James's vision and released on the label that bore the founder's name.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Mary Jane Girls released on Gordy Records (Motown subsidiary). Standard biographical knowledge.

reserve.question: The Mary Jane Girls featured which lead vocalist — known professionally as JoJo — whose voice anchored the group's recording career?

metadata.fact: Joanne 'JoJo' McDuffie was the Mary Jane Girls' primary lead vocalist — the voice most associated with the group's recordings, including 'All Night Long,' 'Candy Man,' and 'In My House.'
metadata.storyHook: JoJo McDuffie. Her voice is the Mary Jane Girls. Four women in the group — but when you think of the sound, you're thinking of her.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: JoJo (Joanne) McDuffie was the Mary Jane Girls' primary lead vocalist. Standard biographical knowledge.

rounds.name: DEEP CUTS
rounds.description: The production machinery, the svengali figures, and the individuals who operated outside the system.

questions.question: Klymaxx was founded and led by which drummer — who handled the group's creative direction and business decisions while serving as its driving force?

metadata.fact: Bernadette Cooper founded Klymaxx, played drums, and served as the group's primary creative and business director — embodying the self-directed model that made Klymaxx the decade's most striking counterpoint to the svengali-produced girl groups around them.
metadata.storyHook: Bernadette Cooper built Klymaxx. She played drums. She ran the group. She answered to nobody. That was the whole point.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Bernadette Cooper was Klymaxx's founder, drummer, and creative director. Standard biographical knowledge.

questions.question: Before achieving fame as The Weather Girls, Martha Wash and Izora Armstead performed under which earlier group name — working as backing vocalists for a Bay Area disco performer?

metadata.fact: Martha Wash and Izora Armstead performed as Two Tons O' Fun before becoming The Weather Girls — working as backing vocalists for San Francisco disco performer Sylvester, whose stage they shared before launching their own career.
metadata.storyHook: Two Tons O' Fun. That was the name before Weather Girls. Martha Wash and Izora Armstead, backing somebody else — building the vocal power that would make 'It's Raining Men' inevitable.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Weather Girls previously performed as Two Tons O' Fun, backing Sylvester. Standard biographical knowledge.

questions.question: Klymaxx demonstrated their range beyond party tracks with which 1984 ballad — a lush, aching recording that became a significant R&B hit and showcased a completely different side of the group?

metadata.fact: 'I Miss You' (1984) was Klymaxx's ballad showcase — a significant commercial and artistic departure from 'Meeting in the Ladies Room' that demonstrated the group's full range as both performers and songwriters.
metadata.storyHook: 'Meeting in the Ladies Room' was the party. 'I Miss You' was the morning after. Klymaxx could do both — and they wrote every note of each.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'I Miss You' was a 1984 R&B hit ballad for Klymaxx. Standard biographical knowledge.

questions.question: When Vanity 6 was reconstituted as Apollonia 6, Prince retained two of the original members — including which vocalist who appeared in both groups?

metadata.fact: Brenda Bennett was one of two members (alongside Susan Moonsie) who carried over from Vanity 6 to Apollonia 6 when Denise Matthews departed — providing continuity in the group's personnel as Prince rebuilt the project for Purple Rain.
metadata.storyHook: When Vanity left, Brenda Bennett stayed. Vanity 6 became Apollonia 6 — and Brenda Bennett was the thread connecting both versions of the project.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Brenda Bennett (and Susan Moonsie) carried over from Vanity 6 to Apollonia 6. Standard biographical knowledge.

questions.question: Miami-based Exposé scored their biggest ballad moment with which 1987 recording — a departure from their freestyle dance sound that reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100?

metadata.fact: 'Seasons Change' (1987) reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 on February 20, 1988 — a dramatic departure from Exposé's uptempo freestyle style and their biggest commercial moment, proving the trio's range well beyond the dance floor.
metadata.storyHook: Exposé made their name on the dance floor. 'Seasons Change' was the moment they proved there was more. 1987 — and the ballad crossed over.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Seasons Change' reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 on February 20, 1988. Sources: Exposé Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expos%C3%A9_(group), Facebook post https://www.facebook.com/FlashBackToTheEightes/posts/on-february-20-1988-the-single-seasons-change-by-expos%C3%A9-reached-1-on-t

questions.question: Before becoming The Weather Girls, Martha Wash and Izora Armstead — as Two Tons O' Fun — were the backing vocalists for which legendary San Francisco disco performer?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 2 OF 3 — THE DISCO ARTIST THE WEATHER GIRLS BACKED BEFORE GOING SOLO

metadata.fact: Martha Wash and Izora Armstead performed as Two Tons O' Fun — the backing vocal duo for San Francisco disco legend Sylvester — before launching their own career as The Weather Girls with 'It's Raining Men.'
metadata.storyHook: Sylvester. San Francisco. The disco stage he built was the stage that made Martha Wash and Izora Armstead. Two Tons O' Fun backed him — then they outgrew the role.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Two Tons O' Fun (later The Weather Girls) backed Sylvester in San Francisco. Standard biographical knowledge.

reserve.question: The Jets — the Tongan-American family group from Minneapolis — topped the Hot R&B chart in 1988 with which recording?

metadata.fact: 'Make It Real' topped the Hot R&B chart for The Jets in 1988 — the commercial peak of a Tongan-American family group from Minneapolis whose ethnic background and Midwestern origin made them one of 1980s pop's most distinctive acts.
metadata.storyHook: The Jets. Minneapolis. Tongan-American siblings. 'Make It Real.' #1 R&B. The late 1980s had room for a family group from the most unexpected corner of the pop landscape.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Make It Real' was a major hit for The Jets in 1988. Standard biographical knowledge.

reserve.question: Miami-based Exposé was assembled and produced by which Miami producer — who created the template that launched one of the era's most commercially consistent freestyle acts?

metadata.fact: Lewis Martinee assembled and produced Exposé — creating the Miami freestyle template that drove the group's commercial success and made them the first group to have four Top 10 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 from a debut album.
metadata.storyHook: Lewis Martinee. Miami. He built Exposé from the ground up — and the freestyle sound he created with them became one of the late 1980s' most commercially reliable formulas.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Lewis Martinee created Exposé; they were the first group with four Top 10 Hot 100 hits from a debut album. Source: No Echo interview https://www.noecho.net/interviews/lewis-martinee-producer-expose-pet-shop-boys-debbie-gibson-cover-girls

reserve.question: Vanity 6, Apollonia 6, and Prince's entire protégée creative infrastructure were centered on which American city — an unlikely Midwestern hub that became 1980s pop's most creatively explosive address?

metadata.fact: Prince's entire protégée operation — Vanity 6, Apollonia 6, and the broader Paisley Park creative ecosystem — was rooted in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The city's isolation from the coastal music industry hubs gave Prince the freedom to build something entirely his own.
metadata.storyHook: Minneapolis. Not New York. Not Los Angeles. Prince built his entire world in Minneapolis — and everything that came out of it, including Vanity 6 and Apollonia 6, carried the city's fingerprints.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Prince's creative operations were based in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Standard biographical knowledge.
metadata.hostNote: Prince died April 21, 2016. The question addresses only the geographic fact about his creative operations — not his death.

rounds.name: HIDDEN GEMS
rounds.description: The archival connections hiding inside the decade's most celebrated girl group moments.

questions.question: 'It's Raining Men' by The Weather Girls (1982) was co-written by Paul Jabara and which musician — later famous for decades as the bandleader on The Late Show with David Letterman?

metadata.fact: 'It's Raining Men' was co-written by Paul Jabara and Paul Shaffer — the musician who spent decades as the bandleader on The Late Show with David Letterman. The song's journey from Shaffer's pen to a Weather Girls global hit is one of pop's most unexpected connections.
metadata.storyHook: Paul Shaffer co-wrote 'It's Raining Men.' The Letterman bandleader. The man who spent decades behind a television desk helped write one of the most exuberant anthems in R&B history — and most people have no idea.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'It's Raining Men' was co-written by Paul Shaffer and Paul Jabara. Standard biographical knowledge.

questions.question: Denise Matthews — who performed as Vanity and fronted Vanity 6 — abandoned her music and acting career in the late 1980s to devote herself entirely to which calling?

metadata.fact: Denise Matthews abandoned her music and acting career to become an evangelical Christian minister and preacher — a total break from the provocative persona she had built as Vanity, and one of the 1980s entertainment world's most complete personal transformations.
metadata.storyHook: She was Vanity. She became something else entirely. Denise Matthews walked away from everything that defined her public image — and replaced it with Christian ministry.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Denise Matthews (Vanity) converted to Christianity and became an evangelical minister, abandoning her music and acting career. Standard biographical knowledge.
metadata.hostNote: Denise Matthews (Vanity) died February 15, 2016. The question addresses her documented conversion and ministry work — not her death. Handle with appropriate care in live delivery.

questions.question: In Purple Rain (1984), Prince played a semi-autobiographical musician known by which nickname — the character around whom the film's entire narrative revolves?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — PRINCE'S CHARACTER NAME IN PURPLE RAIN

metadata.fact: Prince's character in Purple Rain (1984) was called 'The Kid' — a semi-autobiographical young musician in Minneapolis navigating family conflict, romance with Apollonia, and artistic ambition. The character anchored the entire film's narrative.
metadata.storyHook: 'The Kid.' That was the name. Prince playing a version of himself in Purple Rain — and Apollonia 6 orbiting his story from the very first scene.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Prince's character in Purple Rain (1984) was named 'The Kid.' Standard biographical knowledge.
metadata.hostNote: Prince died April 21, 2016. The question addresses only his character name in the film — not his death.

reserve.question: Alongside 'Meeting in the Ladies Room' and 'I Miss You,' Klymaxx released which third 1984 charting single — completing a remarkable year of commercial breakthroughs for the all-female band?

metadata.fact: 'The Men All Pause' was Klymaxx's third charting single of 1984 — completing a year in which the all-female band placed three different recordings on the R&B chart, a commercial consistency matched by few of their contemporaries.
metadata.storyHook: Three charting singles in one year. 'Meeting in the Ladies Room.' 'I Miss You.' 'The Men All Pause.' Klymaxx owned 1984 — on their own terms.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'The Men All Pause' was a third Klymaxx charting hit from 1984. Standard biographical knowledge.

reserve.question: The Jets — the Tongan-American siblings who scored multiple pop and R&B hits in the late 1980s — were all members of which family?

metadata.fact: The Jets were the Wolfgramm family — eight Tongan-American siblings from Minneapolis who scored multiple pop and R&B hits in the late 1980s, making them one of the most ethnically distinctive acts in the decade's mainstream pop landscape.
metadata.storyHook: The Wolfgramm family. Tongan-American. From Minneapolis. Eight siblings who hit #1 on the R&B chart. The Jets were one of the most unlikely commercial success stories of the 1980s.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Jets were the Wolfgramm family — Tongan-American siblings from Minneapolis. Standard biographical knowledge.
